subject: Urgent: PrimeBank production latency and 5xx spike — need temporary capacity + remediation
messages:
From: Emily Carson <emily@primebank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency / 5xx spike — PrimeBank inference (high priority)

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a spike in tail latency and a rising 5xx rate on our dedicated pool at ~06:45 PST. Impact: our fraud-detection scoring is delayed (timeouts at our frontend) and a subset of calls are returning 503. This started after a routine overnight model refresh but we have no plan change on our side.

Current impact: ~12% of requests seeing >1.5s extra latency, ~3% 5xx. This is affecting merchant flows across our east coast region. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a GPU pool saturation / reservation shortfall? We are on a reserved Dedicated plan and need this triaged urgently.

Emily Carson
Sr. Infra Eng, PrimeBank
emily@primebank.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. attaching a short trace we pulled from our side (we can share more logs).

Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — PrimeBank inference (high priority)

Thanks Emily — and sorry for the interruption. We saw matching signals on our end (queue depth rising in your dedicated pool, token throughput close to reservation ceiling). Looping in David and Jonas to diagnose root cause and surface fast mitigations.

Immediate asks from our side:
- David/Jonas: quick check on per-slot headroom and whether noisy neighbor or kernel hotpath is the driver.
- Emily: can you confirm whether the model switch included any quantization or longer input sequences?

We will propose a short mitigation (canary fallback to a slightly smaller model variant + temporary burst authorization) in the next 30–60 minutes. Marissa, I may need your help to coordinate approvals for a one-time burst credit / temporary capacity increase.

— Vanessa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 07:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — PrimeBank inference (high priority)

Quick technical readout (initial):
- Observed: Dedicated pool for account PB-2026-07 reached 98% token processing concurrency across 24 slots between 06:30–06:55. Queue depth (per-instance) doubled and the serving runtime started shedding best-effort background batching causing higher per-token latency.
- Error pattern: 503s originate from our pre-proxy when kernel timeouts cross 2s; stack traces point to an L2 kernel path that regresses on longer context windows (seen in the attached kernel-trace.txt).
- Noisy neighbor: no single tenant spike visible — the consumption profile matches PrimeBank's steady increase in avg tokens per request after the model refresh; that likely pushed them past the reservation runway.

Immediate remediation options we can execute now:
1) Canary fallback to the quantized-1 model variant we host (predictable ~20% lower latency). Requires a quick config flip (safe) and a short template update from PrimeBank. Estimated time to cutover: 7–12 minutes.
2) Temporary burst: allow +30% slot burst on PrimeBank's Dedicated allocation for 2 hours. Requires commercial approval from sales/finance (Marissa).
3) Deprioritize best-effort caching on this pool to free up microseconds per token (non-invasive, but may cost ~5–7% unit-efficiency).

I've attached: pool-usage-20260309.csv (current utilization per slot) and kernel-trace.txt.

I'll execute (1) as soon as I get Emily's go-ahead; if customer prefers capacity-first, we can open a burst authorization and enable (2) while we revert model change.

— David
Director, Infrastructure Ops
David Kim | david_kim@redwood.com

Emily — thanks for raising this so quickly and for the trace. We're proposing the following customer-facing plan: 

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
- T+0 (now): Activate canary fallback to quantized-1 (David can flip). This reduces tail latency quickly — do you approve us toggling the model variant?
- T+10m: If latency doesn't fall to acceptable levels, we request approval to enable a +30% temporary burst for 2 hours. This is a one-time commercial authorization (we will reconcile usage to your plan and propose credits if needed).
- T+60m: If the model refresh on your side introduced longer sequences, we recommend pinning a shorter window length or reverting to previous model version while we run an evaluation in parallel.

I've attached the MAP_v1.xlsx with the steps and a proposed language for our procurement team and engineering-runbook. We will also provide a short postmortem within 48 hours.

Please reply with either: "Approve canary" or "Approve canary + burst" and we will act immediately.

— Marissa Cole

Subject: Exec ask: temporary burst credit & short-term capacity authorization for PrimeBank (PB-2026-07)

Jonas/Irene — brief summary and urgent ask for approval:

Summary:
- PrimeBank (reserved Dedicated) experienced a sustained rise in tokens-per-request after an overnight model refresh. Serving runtime hit reservation ceiling, causing queueing and elevated 5xx. David's initial triage points to longer context windows increasing kernel runtime on the L2 path.
- Customer is mission-critical with a high ARR profile; immediate mitigation will be either canary fallback (recommended first) or a +30% temporary capacity burst for 2 hours if the fallback fails.

Ask (requires exec OK, please reply in-line):
1) Approve one-time burst authorization: +30% slots for a 2-hour window (commercial: we will bill at burst rate; CS to propose credit if customer impacted).
2) If (1) is approved, authorize finance to accept down-payment/credit terms as needed and allow ops to enable burst without additional billing hold.

Rationale: avoids customer downtime, preserves SLA tone, and reduces likelihood of a renewal impact. We will follow up with a PSR and a postmortem within 48 hours.

Attachments referenced: pool-usage-20260309.csv, kernel-trace.txt, MAP_v1.xlsx (in thread). Related HubSpot deal: hs-deal-52341 (linked above).

Thanks — urgent.
— Vanessa
